primary_meaning: Jesus Christ as the rejected stone who becomes the cornerstone (foundation of the Church and God's kingdom)

alternatives.meaning: God (the Father) as the Rock/stone of refuge, strength, and salvation
Believers as living stones built into a spiritual house
The messianic kingdom or Christ as the stone that shatters earthly kingdoms and fills the earth (Daniel's stone)
A stumbling stone or rock of offense (Christ rejected by unbelievers)
Hardened human heart (heart of stone) versus a renewed heart
The tablets of the Law or covenant written on stone

notes: In Christian biblical interpretation the dominant and most frequently taught symbolic use of 'stone' is christological (cornerstone/rejected stone/living stone), drawing especially on the NT's explicit application of OT stone texts to Jesus. Related but distinct uses (God as Rock, believers as living stones, Daniel's kingdom-stone) are also standard and widely recognized; they do not displace the primary christological consensus. Purely negative or non-messianic readings are secondary.
